approachQuestion.prompt:
Expand Nested Agenda Items

An agenda is a multilevel doubly linked structure. Each node has value, prev, next and child. Every sibling list is finite and null-terminated with correct prev links; its head.prev is null. child is null or the head of another sibling list. All nodes are disjoint, with no sharing or cycles across any links except reciprocal prev/next. Return one doubly linked list in depth-first order: a node, then its entire child list recursively, then its original next sibling. Clear every child and maintain all prev/next links, with head.prev=null and tail.next=null. Reuse nodes and values; 0 <= n <= 200000 total nodes.

Input: top A -> B -> C; B.child=D -> E; D.child=F (all sibling links reciprocal). Output: A -> B -> D -> F -> E -> C, with matching prev links and all child links null. Empty input returns null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Walk along next. At a node with a child, find the tail of that child's current sibling list, connect that tail to the saved next sibling (repairing its prev), splice the child head after the node (repairing prev), and clear child. Continue along next, processing newly inserted children in the same way.
options.feedback: Splicing puts the child before the saved sibling; later nested splices preserve this depth-first order while both link directions are repaired.

options.text: First recursively collect all nodes in the required depth-first order into an array, then set all prev/next links and clear children using the array.
options.feedback: The collected order is correct, but the full array and recursive stack are avoidable when sibling links can retain the continuation.

options.text: Use a queue of child-list heads and append each full sibling list before processing its children.
options.feedback: For top A -> B with A.child=C, this produces A,B,C instead of required A,C,B.

options.text: Connect each child after its parent and discard the parent's original next sibling reference.
options.feedback: For A -> B with A.child=C, node B becomes unreachable and disappears.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-12-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n is the total node count. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: The main walk visits each node once. A child-tail search scans only that child list before any of its nested children are spliced; disjoint original sibling lists are each tail-scanned at most once. Total scanning is linear, not one whole flattened suffix per node. All n nodes must be visited to clear child fields. Fixed references suffice; no stack or copied output is used.
